newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS sees drop in EU 96/97 sugar export licences.
newsitem.headline: FIRS sees drop in EU 96/97 sugar export licences.

text.p: The European Union may grant licences to export a cumulative 2.425 million tonnes of sugar during the 1996/97 season, which would represent a decline of 110,000 tonnes versus the previous season, French sugar intervention board FIRS predicted on Monday.

"Assuming tonnages granted between May 21 and end July 1997 (the likely closing date for the current tender) will be similar to those granted during the same period for 1996, that is 430,000 tonnes, the volume of licences awarded for the whole of the 1996/97 campaign, may reach 2.425 million tonnes, or 110,000 tonnes less than in 1995/96," FIRS said in its May report.
Under EU regulations exporters are allowed to export more sugar or less sugar than they hold licences for with a limit of five percent.
But FIRS said operators were unlikely to use that clause beyond a one percent upward limit during the current campaign.
"Under these hypotheses, exports of quota sugars in 1996/97 may not exceed 2.6 million tonnes against 2.758 million tonnes in 1995/96," FIRS said.

At its May 21 weekly tender the European Union awarded licences to export a total of 37,500 tonnes of white sugar under export rebates of a maximum of 43.069 Ecus per 100 kilos . This brought rought cumulative tonnage awarded for exports from the 1996/97 crop to 2.033 million tonnes.
